invariants: Every registered repository uses a full immutable reviewed commit SHA and must match the ecosystem lock.
Repository, service, agent and contract identifiers are unique and owner references must resolve.
Service registrations declare API version, contract IDs, capability IDs and authority mode.
Agent registrations declare delegated capabilities and required contract versions; agents never grant themselves authority.
Platform is the sole consequential execution authority; OS, SDK and TADL registrations are authority-free.
Every consumer declares supported contract versions and rejects missing, stale, unknown or incompatible registrations.
A contract version is immutable once published; incompatible changes require a new contract version.
Capability registration is descriptive and does not itself authorize a request; Platform policy and approval checks remain authoritative.
Every repository record identifies its publisher and records identity-verification state without treating identity metadata as execution authority.

Every repository, service, agent and contract has an explicit active, quarantined, revoked or deprecated lifecycle state; quarantine and revocation fail closed, and deprecation must identify a replacement.

Repository supply-chain metadata carries immutable reviewed SHA plus provenance, SBOM and signature/attestation references; verification status is explicit and pending references are not represented as verified.
Only an independently verified attestation can change supply-chain verification status to verified; registry metadata alone never establishes cryptographic trust.
